prerequisites: Knowledge of the contents of basic subjects from the first and second years, as well as the more technological subjects in the Mechanical Technology area.
Elementary knowledge of Economics, Mechanical Technology, and Manufacturing Processes.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.

syllabus_topics: The Genesis of an Industrial Plant
The Stages of Realizing an Industrial Plant. Objectives of Each Stage
The Implementation of the Industrial Plant
The Land for Installing the Industry
The Structural System in Industrial Buildings
The Foundations of the Industrial Building
Enclosures and Pavements in Industrial Buildings
Compilation of Applicable Legislation for Industrial Plants
Application of the Technical Building Code
teaching_methods: Reading and understanding basic bibliography text
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 20% from the average score of the Continuous Assessment Tests (PECs) and 80% from the in-person exam grade. A minimum exam score of 0 is required for the PEC grade to be considered. If only the exam is considered, a minimum score of 6 out of 10 is needed to pass.
